title: Summary, review and chapter test
competency: Review the unit and take the timed chapter test.

keywords.def: Data sets so massive and complex that typical data processing software or database tools cannot easily process them.
Storing and accessing data and computing services (servers, storage, networking, databases, software) over the Internet, on demand.
A decentralized computing layer where data, computing, storage and applications sit between the data source and the cloud.
A network of physical objects ("things") with sensors, software and electronics that collect and exchange data over the Internet.
Virtualized computing resources (servers, storage, network) rented over the Internet.
A cloud platform (servers, storage, network, OS and middleware, tools) on which developers build, test and host applications.
Finished applications hosted by a provider and used by end users over the Internet, usually by subscription.
A global computer network of interconnected networks using standardized communication protocols.

en.text: Bigdata is massive, complex data described by five V's, with benefits, applications and challenges. Cloud computing delivers data and computing services over the Internet: four types (public, private, hybrid, community) and three services (SaaS, PaaS, IaaS). Fog computing extends the cloud with nodes near the data source to cut latency. The Internet of Things connects sensor-equipped things through four components: sensors, connectivity, data processing and user interface.

screens.text: Review Part I Q1: which statement about Bigdata is NOT correct?
opts: Bigdata is processed using conventional data processing techniques
Bigdata keeps growing exponentially with time
Bigdata includes data mining, storage, analysis, sharing and visualization
Bigdata includes data and data frameworks
screens.ans: Bigdata is processed using conventional data processing techniques
screens.why: Bigdata is "challenging to process using typical data processing software".

screens.text: Review Part III Q3: which are Bigdata uses in education?
pool: Personalised learning plans from grades and attention spans

screens.clue: One use belongs to another sector.

screens.why: p.46: fog computing is an extension of the cloud; fog nodes push the data that needs it on to the cloud.

screens.text: Review Part IV: a group plans IoT for a local health centre storing vaccines at 2–8 °C. Which plan includes all four IoT components?

screens.ans: Fridge temperature sensors → Wi-Fi or cellular → cloud checks 2–8 °C → SMS and dashboard
screens.why: Sense, send, process, then alert: the four components of 2.4.2.

items.text: Q I.1: Which is not correct about basic views of Bigdata?
opts: Bigdata is processed or analyzed using conventional data processing techniques
Bigdata refers to a massive amount of data that keeps on growing exponentially with time
Bigdata includes data mining, data storage, data analysis, data sharing, and data visualization
Bigdata is an all-comprehensive one including data and data frameworks
items.ans: Bigdata is processed or analyzed using conventional data processing techniques
items.why: p.30: Bigdata is challenging for typical data processing software.

items.text: Q I.2: Which characteristic of Bigdata refers to the speed at which data is created in real time?
Q I.3: As IoT exposes a huge amount of detailed personal information, it could create many privacy issues.
items.why: p.50: security and privacy is an IoT limitation.
items.clue: What data do IoT devices collect?

items.why: p.51–52: data processing, not word processing.

items.text: Q III.1: What is the aim of IoT?
opts: To extend Internet connectivity beyond computers and smartphones to everyday things
To replace all computers with paper
To store music in the cloud
items.ans: To extend Internet connectivity beyond computers and smartphones to everyday things

items.text: Q III.4: Mention common advantages of fog computing.
pool: Better mobility and closeness to users
a: Better mobility and closeness to users
items.why: p.46–47. Fog extends the cloud; it does not replace it.

items.text: Q IV (b): which technologies might a health-centre IoT project need?
pool: A cloud or local fog server
A phone dashboard and SMS alerts
a: A cloud or local fog server
A phone dashboard and SMS alerts
items.why: These cover the four components of 2.4.2.
